rationale: Left ventricular ejection fraction is a percentage; a value above 100 means a fraction was multiplied twice or a different quantity was mapped here.
Resting heart rate in counts per minute.
Systolic blood pressure in mmHg.
Diastolic blood pressure in mmHg.
Body weight in kilograms; the lower bound catches weights recorded in stones or pounds.
Body height in centimetres; values below 100 usually mean metres were reported.
Haemoglobin in grams per litre; values below 20 usually mean grams per decilitre were reported.
Serum creatinine in milligrams per decilitre; values above 20 usually mean micromoles per litre were reported.
NT-proBNP in picograms per millilitre. The upper bound is deliberately permissive; extreme values occur in decompensated heart failure.
CHA2DS2-VASc is an integer score with a maximum of 9. Unitless.
CHA2DS2-VA is the sex-agnostic variant of CHA2DS2-VASc and drops the sex category, so its maximum is 8. Unitless.
HAS-BLED is an integer score with a maximum of 9. Unitless.

AF burden is a proportion of monitored time expressed as a percentage; values outside 0-100 indicate the site reported hours or a fraction instead. Only valid within an aggregated burden window (Case A), since it summarises AF time over a continuous monitoring period rather than a single episode.
Fraction of days in sinus rhythm, expressed as a percentage over the monitoring window. Only valid within an aggregated burden window (Case A).
Number of analysable ECGs in the monitoring period; denominator for intermittent AF-burden estimation. Only valid within an aggregated burden window (Case A).

Number of ECGs classified as AF in the monitoring period; numerator for intermittent AF-burden estimation. Must not exceed the corresponding N_ECG_TOTAL value. Only valid within an aggregated burden window (Case A).

Duration of a single arrhythmia episode in seconds. Only valid within a disaggregated episode (Case B). No upper bound: AF episodes can persist for days before resolving or transitioning into a monitored window. Lower bound of 0 catches negative or malformed values.

Maximum atrial or ventricular rate during an arrhythmia episode. Generous bounds intended to catch unit and transcription errors, not to define clinical normality. Only valid within a disaggregated episode (Case B), since a peak rate describes a single event, not a multi-day window.

AFEQT (Atrial Fibrillation Effect on QualiTy-of-life) total score, normalized from 7-point Likert-scale items to a 0-100 range (higher = better quality of life). Unitless, like the other composite scores. Not scoped to a specific episode type, since it reflects overall patient-reported burden rather than a single monitoring window or episode.
Longest AF episode duration in seconds within the window. No upper bound (see 2000009003 rationale).
Shortest AF episode duration in seconds within the window.
Mean AF episode duration in seconds within the window.
SD of AF episode duration in seconds within the window.
Mean ventricular rate during AF in counts per minute, same bounds as peak rate (2000009004).
SD of mean ventricular rate during AF in counts per minute.
Total beat count within a single AF episode. Unitless (count), no upper bound.
Count of discrete AF episodes within the window. Unitless, no upper bound.
Absolute AF duration in seconds within the window. No upper bound.
Percent atrial paced.
Percent ventricular paced.
AT/AF shock count. Unitless.
VT/VF shock count. Unitless.
Daily device-measured activity duration in seconds; upper bound is a full day (86400 s).
Fluid status threshold crossing count. Unitless.
Daily spontaneous NST episode count. Unitless.
PVC burden as percent of total beats.
Daily thoracic impedance in ohms. No upper bound; devices typically report values in the hundreds of ohms.
Accumulated thoracic impedance deviation in ohms, cumulative over time. No upper bound.
Reference thoracic impedance baseline in ohms.
R-R interval mean, milliseconds.
R-R interval maximum, milliseconds.
R-R interval minimum, milliseconds.
R-R interval standard deviation (heart rate variability), milliseconds.
Daytime resting heart rate, counts per minute.
Nighttime resting heart rate, counts per minute.
Max heart rate during AF within window, counts per minute.
